title: Shorten the edit-and-observe loop
purpose: A slow rebuild-and-deploy loop interrupts experimentation. For developers already comfortable running TraderX on Kubernetes, use Tilt to connect a local change to a running workload and distinguish the last successful deployment from the latest attempted edit.
entryAssumptions: The Kubernetes state requires explicit build and deployment steps for changes.
concepts: A reconciliation loop tries to make running resources match desired configuration. File watching can trigger updates, but an update finishing does not prove the changed behavior.
runtimePrerequisites: Use the state quickstart for tool versions, generation, start and stop commands. Run one local state at a time because ports and generated output directories are shared.

transitions.carriesForward: Run C2 on Kubernetes and explain ingress, service routing and pod readiness.
transitions.motivation: The Kubernetes state requires explicit build and deployment steps for changes.
transitions.increment: Use Tilt to orchestrate the local Kubernetes development loop.
transitions.evidence: The loop connects a local edit with a rebuilt or updated workload. Record which resource changed and how long it took; do not assume every edit uses live update. A failed rebuild can leave the old application serving. A responsive browser is therefore insufficient evidence that the latest edit deployed.

objectives.outcome: Correlate a local edit, its Tilt resource update and the visible application version.
Explain the evidence boundary: A failed rebuild can leave the old application serving. A responsive browser is therefore insufficient evidence that the latest edit deployed.

walkthrough.action: Follow the state quickstart and inspect the generated Tiltfile and watched paths. In a disposable generated checkout make a visible UI text change, observe the Tilt resource update, and reload the UI to verify that the change reached the browser.
walkthrough.expected: The loop connects a local edit with a rebuilt or updated workload. Record which resource changed and how long it took; do not assume every edit uses live update.

walkthrough.action: Introduce a reversible syntax error in that disposable file, observe the build error, then undo it. Check whether the browser still shows the previous successful version while the new build fails.
walkthrough.expected: A failed rebuild can leave the old application serving. A responsive browser is therefore insufficient evidence that the latest edit deployed.

assessments.question: How can you prove the browser is serving your latest edit?
assessments.guidance: Correlate the successful Tilt update with the exact visible change. Explain why a failed build and a healthy old pod can coexist.

limitations: A failed rebuild can leave the old application serving. A responsive browser is therefore insufficient evidence that the latest edit deployed.
This is an educational local demonstration. Passing its checks does not establish production readiness, financial settlement, or correctness under every failure mode.
